asset_name: CMAB015 (new-process secukinumab biosimilar; Secukinumab 150 mg s.c.)
mechanism: Secukinumab is an IL-17A-targeting monoclonal antibody. CMAB015 is a candidate biosimilar to Cosentyx that is intended to match secukinumab in structure, pharmacokinetics, safety, and immunogenicity rather than provide a new mechanism.
phase: Assigned study is Phase 1; broader CMAB015 psoriasis program has a completed Phase 3 study.
development_status: Active, not recruiting in the assigned Phase 1 new-process PK/safety/immunogenicity bridging study. The related Phase 3 plaque psoriasis equivalence trial is completed, and Mabpharm/Taizhou Mabtech states it expects to file an NDA for CMAB015 in China in Q3 2026 with potential NMPA marketing approval in Q1 2028.
clinical_summary: NCT07254325 is a 114-subject, randomized, triple-masked, single-dose Phase 1 study in healthy Chinese male volunteers comparing new-process CMAB015 150 mg s.c. with reference Cosentyx 150 mg s.c.; primary endpoints are AUC0-inf and Cmax through 2688 hours, with no results posted. Earlier CMAB015 Phase 1 data in 130 healthy Chinese male subjects met bioequivalence margins for Cmax and AUC0-inf versus secukinumab. The completed Phase 3 plaque psoriasis study enrolled 336 adults and tested PASI 75 equivalence at Week 12, but results are not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
safety_summary: NCT07254325 has no posted safety results. In the published earlier Phase 1 CMAB015 study, safety and immunogenicity were similar to secukinumab, with no treatment-related serious adverse events, no allergic reactions, no injection-site reactions, and low ADA positivity. Cosentyx labeling highlights infection risk, TB evaluation, IBD caution, hypersensitivity, eczematous eruptions, and avoidance of live vaccines; common adult psoriasis adverse reactions include nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, and upper respiratory tract infection.
management_tools: Preferred biosimilar or lowest-net-cost formulary placement after contracting review
Step therapy aligned to moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis criteria
Dose and quantity limits tied to labeled 150 mg or 300 mg subcutaneous regimens
Continuation criteria based on PASI, BSA, IGA, or documented symptom improvement
Nonmedical switching policy with prescriber override for clinical exceptions
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT07254325.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for the completed Phase 3 CMAB015 plaque psoriasis trial NCT06398652.
No CMAB015 commercial price or net contracting assumptions are available.
The company source describes an expected NMPA path in China; U.S. or EU regulatory timing is not established.
The assigned study is a healthy-volunteer PK bridging study and does not directly measure psoriasis efficacy.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetic, Safety and Immunogenicity Study of New Process CMAB015 and Cosentyx in Healthy Volunteers
supports: Assigned study is active, not recruiting; sponsor is Taizhou Mabtech Pharmaceutical Co.,Ltd.
Randomized, triple-masked Phase 1 study enrolling an estimated 114 healthy Chinese male volunteers.
Compares new-process CMAB015 150 mg subcutaneous injection with Cosentyx 150 mg subcutaneous injection.
Primary endpoints are AUC0-inf and Cmax through 2688 hours; no results are posted.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetic, Safety and Immunogenicity Study of CMAB015 and Cosentyx in Healthy Volunteers
supports: Earlier completed Phase 1 CMAB015 study sponsored by Taizhou Mabtech Pharmaceutical Co.,Ltd.
Enrolled 130 healthy Chinese male subjects and compared single-dose CMAB015 150 mg s.c. with Cosentyx 150 mg s.c.
ClinicalTrials.gov references the published Drug Design, Development and Therapy report.

sources.title: Comparative Study of CMAB015 and Secukinumab for Patients With Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis
supports: Completed Phase 3, randomized, double-blind equivalence study in 336 adult patients with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis.
Compared CMAB015 300 mg s.c. with secukinumab 300 mg s.c. through Week 52.
Primary endpoint was PASI 75 at Week 12 with an equivalence cutoff of +/-15%; no results are posted.

sources.title: Mabpharm Limited 2025 Annual Report
supports: CMAB015 is described as a biosimilar candidate for secukinumab targeting IL-17A.
Company says Phase 1 is complete, Phase 3 enrollment was completed during the reporting period, and Phase 3 would soon complete.
Company expects to file an NDA for CMAB015 in Q3 2026 and says NMPA marketing approval may occur in Q1 2028.

sources.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group Phase I Study Comparing the Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Immunogenicity of CMAB015, a Candidate Secukinumab Biosimilar, with Its Reference Product Cosentyx in Healthy Chinese Male Subjects
supports: CMAB015 is a candidate secukinumab biosimilar developed by Taizhou Mabtech Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
The published Phase 1 study randomized 130 healthy Chinese male subjects to single-dose CMAB015 150 mg s.c. or secukinumab 150 mg s.c.
Cmax and AUC0-inf geometric mean ratio confidence intervals were within 80.00%-125.00% bioequivalence limits.
Safety and immunogenicity were comparable, with no treatment-related serious adverse events.

sources.title: COSENTYX (secukinumab) Prescribing Information
supports: Cosentyx is approved for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.
Adult plaque psoriasis dosing is 300 mg s.c. at Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 and every 4 weeks thereafter; 150 mg may be acceptable for some patients.
Secukinumab selectively binds IL-17A and inhibits interaction with the IL-17 receptor.
Warnings include serious infections, TB evaluation, IBD caution, hypersensitivity, eczematous eruptions, and live-vaccine avoidance.

sources.title: Paying for COSENTYX
supports: As of January 2026, Cosentyx list or wholesale price is $8,492.03 per month for either a 150 mg or 300 mg self-injection package.
The manufacturer notes that list price may not reflect patient-paid amounts.

sources.title: FDA and FTC Collaborate to Advance Competition in the Biologic Marketplace
supports: FDA states that a biosimilar is highly similar to and has no clinically meaningful differences from the reference biologic.
FDA cites market evidence that biosimilar average sales price is less than half the reference product price at launch.

sources.title: Biosimilar Product Information
supports: FDA list of approved biosimilars is current as of May 15, 2026.
The list supports that FDA-approved biosimilar products are tracked by reference product and did not establish a CMAB015 or secukinumab biosimilar approval in the reviewed source.

sources.title: Secukinumab (Cosentyx) - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin 0905
supports: Commercial payer analog uses prescriber-specialty requirements, plaque psoriasis severity criteria, TB screening, no concomitant biologic use, and continuation based on clinical response.
Policy includes step-through criteria for some secukinumab use and dose language aligned to FDA labeling.

expected_launch_window.method: Used Mabpharm annual-report guidance for expected China NDA and NMPA timing.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The company states it expects CMAB015 NDA filing in Q3 2026 and possible NMPA marketing approval in Q1 2028; no U.S. or EU launch timing was identified.

annual_cost_range.method: High estimate uses Cosentyx 2026 U.S. list price of $8,492.03 per month multiplied by 12. Low estimate applies a 50% biosimilar discount proxy to the reference-product annual maintenance list price, based on FDA-cited biosimilar ASP experience.
annual_cost_range.explanation: CMAB015 has no disclosed commercial price. Range is an analog U.S. acquisition estimate for ongoing maintenance and excludes loading-dose variation, rebates, patient cost share, administration, monitoring, and country-specific China pricing.

clinical_differentiation.method: Assigned low differentiation because CMAB015 is a biosimilar candidate intended to match secukinumab rather than improve efficacy, safety, dosing, or mechanism.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Published Phase 1 data support PK similarity to Cosentyx; the completed Phase 3 equivalence trial has no posted results, and biosimilar value is expected to be access/cost rather than clinical superiority.

budget_impact.method: Balanced high per-patient biologic cost and broad psoriasis use against likely displacement of reference-product spend by a biosimilar.
budget_impact.explanation: A secukinumab biosimilar could create savings if preferred, but biologic psoriasis therapy remains high cost and may require contracting and utilization controls.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed from near-term biosimilar timing, possible formulary switching, and payer management changes for a high-spend immunology biologic.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational disruption is more likely in formulary, contracting, and switching policy than in clinical pathway redesign because the product is not clinically differentiated from Cosentyx.

recommended_action.method: Recommended preparation because company-guided NMPA timing is within the planning horizon and Phase 3 is completed, while pricing and final results remain unavailable.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin biosimilar readiness work around lowest-net-cost positioning, switching rules, and prior authorization criteria; defer active implementation until approval, label, price, and Phase 3 results are available.

quality_flags: Biosimilar/process-change bridging study: CMAB015 is not a novel mechanism, and the reference product Cosentyx (secukinumab) is already marketed/approved.
Assigned NCT07254325 is a healthy-volunteer PK/safety/immunogenicity study, not a psoriasis patient efficacy trial, despite psoriasis being listed as the condition.
NCT07254325 has no posted results as of 2026-05-28.
Related Phase 3 psoriasis study NCT06398652 is completed but has no posted results as of 2026-05-28.
Expected launch timing is company-guided for China/NMPA; U.S. or EU regulatory path and timing were not established.
CMAB015 commercial price is undisclosed; annual cost estimate is analog-derived from Cosentyx U.S. list price and general biosimilar discount evidence.
